Thanks Olga — quick summary from our side: Acme wants the on-prem Redwood control plane to expose two private hostnames (api.internal.acme-fin.com and embed.internal.acme-fin.com) over our VPC. Our security team requires mutual TLS for any control-plane <-> customer ingress, audit logs for cert usage, and ability to rotate leaf certs without downtime. We cannot use publicly trusted ACME for these names.

Questions:
- Can Redwood terminate TLS at the customer edge proxy (we run F5/Envoy) and still preserve token-level tracing?
- Do you have an expected cert-chain format (chain, intermediate, root) we must accept for mutual auth?

Action items from Acme: we attached our checklist and a short network sketch (attached). Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk through constraints tomorrow.

—Kara

Subject: Re: Split DNS and mutual TLS handoff for private endpoints

Kara — thanks for the checklist and sketch. High-level responses and assumptions below. I'll loop Hiro and Marissa for cert/runtime details and Karthik for VPC routing.

Summary assumptions:
- Private hostnames will be reachable only from Acme VPCs/subnets and via the customer edge proxy (Envoy/F5).
- Redwood will not request public certs for these hostnames. Mutual TLS will use customer-managed CA (can be internal PKI).
- We must support rolling leaf cert replacement with no dropped in-flight requests and enable automatic health-based fallback to a hosted variant if the private endpoint becomes unavailable.

Short answers to your questions:
- TLS termination options: we support three patterns: (1) terminate mTLS at customer edge and forward via mTLS or plain TLS to Redwood per policy; (2) pass-through TCP (SNI) to an on-prem edge service that terminates; (3) full mutual TLS end-to-end where Redwood verifies client certs and presents a server cert signed by the customer's internal CA. Option (3) is preferred for end-to-end identity and per-token auditability but has higher operational footprint.
- Cert format: Redwood expects PEM-formatted chains (leaf + intermediates). For mutual auth we validate client cert CN/SAN and check chain against the provided trust anchor(s). We support CRL/OCSP checks if Acme provides network access to your OCSP responder.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Hiro will draft a cert validation & OCSP/CRL integration design.
2) Marissa will outline runtime configuration (SNI, ALPN, and header passthrough for tracing).
3) Karthik to provide VPC route table & proxy ingress constraints (NAT/gateway, port mapping).
4) Sync call: Tue 2027-04-12 10:00 PT — propose 30m to review.

I'm attaching our internal playbook snippets for cert rotation.

Olga

On Tue, Apr 12, 2027 at 10:00 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sync call notes attached — below are the engineering points we committed to follow up on.

Engineering notes: 
- mTLS verification modes: server-side can be configured to either (A) validate client certs against a pinned root CA bundle (recommended), or (B) accept any client cert and defer authorization to tokens in the request. We should default to (A) for Acme.
- Certificate presentation: Redwood can present either a Redwood-managed leaf cert signed by Acme's subordinate CA (you sign a CSR) OR Acme can upload their own server cert and private key (stored in KMS/HSM). For security/compliance, customer-uploaded keys should be stored in a customer-managed HSM when on Private deployments.
- Key rollover: support for double-write TTL — we accept both old and new certs for a configurable overlap window (default: 36 hours) to avoid handoff failures. We'll add health-check probes to the routing tier to detect failures during rollover.
- OCSP stapling: if Acme's infra can provide stapled responses at the proxy layer, Redwood will consume stapled responses; otherwise we will fetch OCSP from the responder if network egress is permitted.

Open engineering questions for Acme:
1) Can you provide your root CA bundle in PEM? (we need fingerprints)
2) Do you require SPIFFE identities or is CN/SAN matching sufficient?
3) Which proxies will terminate SNI (customer edge vs on-prem edge service)? If the customer edge terminates and strips client certs, we will lose mTLS identity upstream — need to confirm header passthrough options.

I'll produce a short PRD for the cert validation flow by EOD Wednesday.

—Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Split DNS and mutual TLS handoff for private endpoints

Thanks everyone for the clear plan. A few clarifications and requests from security: 
- We will provide a PEM-formatted root bundle and a signing policy. We'll prefer Redwood to verify client certs directly (mode A).
- For server certs we want to keep private keys in our HSM. Kara asked whether Redwood on Private mode can authenticate to a customer HSM via PKCS#11 — Kara: yes, we have an HSM appliance reachable from the on-prem cluster.
- Auditability: Acme needs request-level cert fingerprint logged in access logs and available in the Console (redacted token info is fine).

Operational asks: 
- Please include a short runbook for cert rollover (we saw Hiro's overlap approach; please include curl/openssl checks we can run).
- Can Redwood provide a fallback policy that routes to a hosted Redwood endpoint (read-only) if the private endpoint fails health checks for >5 minutes? We need an SLA mapping for that fallback window.

We're fine with the proposed 36-hour overlap window. Attached is a redacted example of our root bundle and a short network map. We'll get you HSM access details over the secure channel next week.

Next: Hiro/Marissa — update PRD + runtime config, add the runbook steps and the logging keys. We can aim to sign off on April 20 if all looks good.

—Kara
